newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma says considering sanctions against EU.
newsitem.headline: Burma says considering sanctions against EU.

text.p: Burma's foreign minister Ohn Gyaw said on Friday the country is considering imposing reciprocal sanctions against the European Union after the EU slapped strict limits on contacts with Burmese officials earlier this week.

"The EU, I believe, is very one-sided in its approach," Ohn Gyaw said at the monthly news conference given by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC). "We are saying leave us alone, it is our internal affiars. Our response will be on a reciprocal basis."
Ohn Gyaw said he had not yet decided when reciprocal measures would be imposed. "It will be decided by the Minister of Foreign Affairs. When we need it we will do it."

On Monday EU foreign ministers ageed without debate to impose strict limits on contacts with SLORC officials and their families. The new sanctions bar visas to SLORC members and their families and suspend high-level EU visits to Burma.
Ohn Gyaw said a reciprocal move may not be made against all 15 EU member nations. "When we take action it may or may not be to all because most of the EU members are our friends," he said.

The United States took a similar move last month. Diplomats say the restrictions are part of a gradual build-up of pressure on Rangoon's military government, its poor human rights record and failure to enter into dialogue with the pro-democracy movement led by Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.
